dedupe_keys.name: hong kong international airport cost benefit analysis of micro waste to energy incinerators

description: This case study tests whether small waste-to-energy incinerators installed within a city can be financially viable, using the Hong Kong International Airport as the application site. Fuhao Zu and Xueqing Zhang of the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology published it in Waste Management in 2023. They propose a cost-benefit method for micro incinerators with two energy recovery options and convert the carbon emission reduction compared with the existing disposal route into money through a carbon trading system. Two facilities with different technologies, low-temperature magnetisation and high-temperature pyrolysis gasification, are analysed under six application scenarios with different benefit mixes, followed by a sensitivity analysis. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution Non Commercial No Derivatives licence. Coverage is one airport site. Caveats: benefits depend strongly on carbon prices and energy recovery assumptions, and site data are not published separately. The results show strong potential for micro waste-to-energy incinerators in urban settings, with the low-temperature magnetisation facility ahead of the pyrolysis gasification one. Simulation uses: costs, benefits and scenario structure for decentralised waste treatment options in urban waste system models. Related records: the Nova Scotia waste-to-energy capacity planning study (case_study-nova-scotia-waste-to-energy-technology-capacity-planning) appraises larger plants.
